answer: Fresh-pair coordination billing uses a jade receipt for every new counterpart pair. Both identities must pay a nonrefundable 0.01-unit fee when a vine records a first-time joint action; repeat pairs are free. A mirror audit compares both logs before settlement, and failed checks forfeit the epoch’s fees. An attacker faking k identities and m peers pays 0.01·k·m plus audit forfeitures, so broad coordination becomes the expensive part.
